spans.s: मृदु (1) soft in utterance ; the term is used in the Vaajasaneyi Praatisaakhya for the क्षेप्र, प्रश्लिष्ट, तैरोन्यञ्जन, and पादवृत्त varieties of the circumflex accent (स्वरित) out ofwhich the पादवृत्त is the softest ( मृदुतम ) and conse- guently always called मृदु, while the others are called मृदु only with respect to the preceding one in the order given above; viz.अभिनिहृत, क्षैप्र etc.cf.सर्वतीक्ष्णोभिनिहृत: प्राश्लिष्टस्तदनन्तरम् । ततो मृदुतरौ स्वरौ जात्यक्षेप्रावुभौ स्मृतौ | ततेी मृदुतंर: स्वारस्तैरोन्यञ्जन उच्यते | पांदवृत्तो मृदुतमस्त्वेतत्स्वारबलाबलम् Uvvata on V.Pr. I. !25; (2) soft, as opposed to hard; the term is used in connection with the first,third and fifth consonants of the five classcs.
